body:
# the contributor audit: quantitative contact rigidity and moving-body continuity

Source read in full:
`candidate b2439018eaa1681d`.

No derivative of the optimized value or sharp body payment follows.

The fixed-body estimate uses Jensen under the actual tilted rows to bound
the ORIGINAL expectation of U/L. Log normalization gives the reverse
lower bound one. The stated orientation of relative entropy is correct:
KL(P_0 || (U/L)P_0/b)=log b. The proof of the Pinsker convention has the
correct factor two. The L1-to-interior estimate follows from the uniform
concave-function slope bound and a ball on which an observed discrepancy
retains at least half its value. Its radius stays inside the claimed
interior core because the discrepancy is at most the sum of the maxima.
The normalized interval example has exactly the stated logarithmic
integral and correctly excludes sampled-boundary uniform convergence.

The reference competitor on changing domains is legitimate. The affine
homothety maps C_m into C by the displayed support inequality. It is used
only to compose the PARAMETER, not to move integer fibers or claim depth
invariance. Positivity and uniform continuity of the old L justify its
normalizing factor. The fixed-base all-direction slab bound treats every
unbounded integer tilt and keeps the pure-base cap masses separately.

The key row-push step is also valid. A common inward factor sends each
old fiber into the corresponding new one. Pushing a row by the possibly
nonaffine-in-z map does not preserve its old continuous mean, and the
source explicitly includes the correction E_(rho_i) g_Z. Its base mean
is unchanged and remains the same INTEGER p_i. Its corrected full mean
belongs to the actual new fiber because the new canonical hull has exactly
the sampled sections. The corrected mark tends to the old interior mark.

The upper value bound for near optimizers, scalar-depth continuity, and
strict proper-buffer monotonicity bound every parameter value at these
corrected marks. Jensen then bounds the pullback integral without any
prior parameter compactness assumption. The maximum estimate on an inner
homothetic fiber and the outer homothetic comparison extend that bound to
the entire new fiber. The Jacobian cancels in the displayed average; no
missing power of 1-t_m occurs in the maximum estimate.

Normalization gives a uniform positive lower bound on each FIBER MAXIMUM,
not a false lower bound on every boundary value. Homothetic superlevels
then bound the volume of {U_m<r} by C r, uniformly. Layer cake gives
C r(1+|log r|) for its logarithmic tail and uniform absolute logarithmic
integrability on arbitrary sets of vanishing volume. Thus the collar
estimate does not assume regular boundaries or positive boundary values
uniformly in m.

The pullback entropy identity is exact because the contraction factor is
the SAME on every fiber. Full new-domain log normalization leaves precisely
the negative collar integral divided by M(1-t_m)^d. Its convergence to zero
and the row upper bound force the pullback relative entropy to zero. The
claimed L1 bound follows, then interior uniform convergence follows by
concavity. Passing from pulled-back coordinates to the same continuous
coordinates uses a uniform interior slope bound; it does not assert that
the nonaffine row-push is a valid global body transformation.

Finally, small collars and the logarithmic uniform-integrability bound
justify both zero-extension L1 conclusions. The logarithm is extended by
zero as a function, not taken after extending U by zero. Uniform boundedness
of the parameters and the energy's boundary zero justify uniform convergence
of buffers despite the false boundary-uniform parameter statement. The
all-normal slab comparison then gives convergence of the actual maxima,
or equivalently the reference upper bound and a corrected old source give
matching upper and lower limits.

This proves the stated continuity for arbitrary o(1)-optimal sequences;
existence of exact optimizers along the perturbed bodies was neither needed
nor assumed. It supplies neither an O(t) parameter estimate nor a derivative
interchange for a body path. Any use of those stronger assertions would
require an additional argument.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
